# Benchmarking Multi‑LLM Visibility in 2026: Standards, Sampling, and Industry Benchmarks

The rapid shift from keyword‑based search to answer‑engine experiences has made it essential to measure how brands surface across multiple large language model (LLM) platforms, including ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Gemini, Grok, Microsoft Copilot, and Mistral Le Chat.[7][17][38] In 2026, this visibility is no longer a soft branding metric but a measurable driver of discovery, pipeline, and revenue, particularly in verticals where AI Overviews and conversational assistants now mediate a large share of information‑seeking behavior.[7][13][39] This report develops a rigorous benchmarking framework for multi‑LLM presence that integrates GEO (generative engine optimization) theory, share‑of‑voice measurement, and modern observability practices. It proposes standardized sampling designs that control for personalization, memory, device, and geography; defines a metric stack that connects input signals, channel‑level visibility, and business outcomes; and synthesizes emerging industry benchmarks by vertical, drawing on datasets from Ahrefs Brand Radar, Profound, iPullRank’s GEO work, Search Engine Land, and independent AI visibility studies.[2][3][7][13][16][26][35][39][43][28] By the end, practitioners should be able to design a defensible, repeatable benchmarking program that compares their brand’s presence across LLMs, tracks change through model updates, and ties AI share of voice back to competitive position and commercial impact.

## 1. The New Discovery Landscape and the Case for Multi‑LLM Benchmarking

### 1.1 From search rankings to model‑mediated discovery

The discovery landscape in 2026 is increasingly mediated by LLMs that answer questions directly, synthesize web content into narrative responses, and selectively cite brands as examples, recommendations, or sources.[7][28][35] Generative engine optimization (GEO) formalizes the idea that brands must now compete not only for positions on search engine results pages (SERPs) but also for inclusion in the small set of domains that LLMs retrieve and synthesize into an answer.[28][28] Search Engine Land’s GEO framework frames this as the shift from earning one of ten blue links to earning a place among the two to seven domains that typically appear in an AI answer panel, including Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT browsing modes, Per
